# Roulette — what it does, in plain language

Roulette is one contract on Kadena Community Edition (kda-chain.org) that runs a European
single-zero wheel. A round opens the moment somebody places the first bet, takes bets for a
fixed window, and is then decided by a random number produced by a group of independent
organisations **outside Kadena entirely**. Nobody runs the round: the players open it, anybody
settles it, and the winners collect.

> **Two different people appear on this page, and the difference matters.**
>
> - **The house** is whoever holds the signing key. It puts capital into the pot, sets the
>   table's limits, and takes the pot's earnings out. It never plays, it sends no transaction
>   inside a round, and it holds no secret of any kind.
> - **A player** is anyone who places a bet. A player needs no permission from the house, and —
>   like anyone at all — can settle a round, keep the refund clock from running, or send a
>   winner's collection for them.
>
> **So "you" on this page always means a player.** The house is never "you"; it is always named.

> 🔴 **Until the contract is locked, the house's key can take the pot.**
>
> Everything below describes the contract's own rules, and that one key is the exception to all
> of them. *What the house can and cannot do* says exactly what it can do instead. The contract
> is not locked today, and locking it ends this for good.

## In one minute

**What it can do**

- ✅ Pay the same share of every KDA staked back to players, on all 158 bets on the table.
- ✅ Take the winning number from a beacon produced away from Kadena, and check its proof on chain.
- ✅ Lock each round to a beacon that does not exist yet, and stop taking bets a fixed wait before it appears.
- ✅ Let anyone settle a round, and pay a winner's money to the winner whoever sends the transaction.
- ✅ Reserve the worst pocket before accepting a bet, so the pot can never fail to pay one it took.
- ✅ Refund a round rather than keep it, if the beacon is ever retired.

**What it cannot do**

- ✅ **Choose or steer the winning number** — the house included. The number is worked out from a
  beacon nobody here produces, and the proof is checked by the contract itself.
- ✅ **Change a round once it has opened.** Its closing time, its beacon, its limit, its minimum and
  what the pot owes on every pocket are all fixed by its first bet.
- ✅ **Take the fee out of your stake.** The fee comes out of the pot, and it only decides how much
  of the pot's own earnings are forwarded rather than kept.
- ✅ **Pause a round, cancel it, or reverse a bet.** There is no pause button, no override and no
  undo: a live round keeps the limits it opened with, it cannot be voided while its beacon can
  still arrive, and nothing is paid out before the wheel has decided — a wrong bet stays wrong,
  and so does a winning one. Stopping *future* rounds is a different thing, and the house can
  (see "What the house can and cannot do", below).
- ✅ **Stop a winner collecting.** Collecting needs nobody's permission and nobody's cooperation.
- ✅ **Recover a lost key.** A lost key is lost: on Kadena an account *is* its key, and winnings can
  only ever be paid to the account that placed the bet — nobody, the house included, can point
  them anywhere else.
- ✅ **Stop the house's key from taking the pot, until the contract is locked.** That is the one
  exception to everything above, and locking the contract is what ends it.

## The money

✅ A player's return is 36/37 — 97.2973% — of everything staked, on every bet the table offers.
✅ One pocket in 37 never pays, and that one pocket is the whole of the house's earnings — 2.7027%.
✅ There is no sucker bet on this table: no bet is worse than another.

✅ The fee is taken from the pot, never from a stake, and can never be more than that one pocket.
✅ The fee is smaller while the pot is below its target, and reaches that ceiling only once the pot is healthy, so a thin pot keeps more of its own earnings and refills.

| Money | Who gets it | When |
|---|---|---|
| **A losing stake** | The pot | The moment the round settles — nobody sends anything |
| **A winning board** | The player who placed it, at the official multiple for every chip that hit | When the player, or anyone at all on their behalf, sends the collection |
| **The fee** | The account the house names at the start | Inside the settling transaction |
| **A refunded round** | Every player, their whole stake back. No fee is taken | When the player, or anyone at all, sends the collection |

✅ The pot reserves the worst pocket of the whole round before it accepts a bet. It can refuse a bet; it can never run short on one it took.
✅ The reserve also covers a full refund of every stake, with the fee inside it.
✅ What the pot has reserved never exceeds what the pot holds, at any point in a round's life.
✅ A loser never sends anything: the pot releases what it reserved the moment the round settles.

**The table limit.**
✅ A round can never put more than the share of the pot's spare capital the house has set.
✅ That share is 2.5% today.
✅ The house can change it at any time, including after the contract is locked.
✅ The contract's own bound on it is arithmetic and nothing else: a share above 100% of the spare capital is refused, because a round cannot risk more than the pot has spare.
✅ The share the contract starts with is below the level at which the bank would stop growing, for every kind of bet the table offers.
✅ Above roughly 5.5% the bank stops growing on the worst of those bets: that is advice the house followed in choosing today's share, not a limit the contract puts on the house.
✅ The limit is measured against the smaller of the pot when the round opened and the pot now.
✅ Money put into the pot mid-round does not widen a table already in play either.
✅ The limit bounds the whole round rather than one player, so a round can fill up and a bet is then refused until the next one.

**The earnings account.**
✅ Where the house's earnings go is fixed once at the start and can never be named again.
✅ Taking money out of the pot can only pay that one account, never one chosen at the time.
✅ Money already reserved against open rounds cannot be taken out.

## A round, step by step

1. **You place a board.**
   ✅ You sign one transaction and nothing else.
   ✅ Every chip goes in that one transaction, and a second board in the same round is refused.
   ✅ The first bet of a round opens it, and fixes the closing time, the beacon, the limit and the minimum for everyone who joins it.
2. **The round takes bets.**
   ✅ A round takes bets for 2 minutes, by the chain's own clock, and not a moment longer.
   ✅ The beacon the round is locked to appears a fixed wait after betting closes, so it does not exist while a bet can still be placed.
   ✅ The contract launched with that wait at 3 minutes; the house's current setting is shown on the play page, read from the chain.
   ✅ The wait before the beacon is the house's setting, and the contract refuses anything under 60 seconds or over 1 hour.
   🟡 That floor is the lowest the setting can go and not a value that is safe to run at — the house runs well above it — because at 60 seconds roughly one round in fourteen would have no block between its close and its beacon, and a watcher could then read the beacon and bet on it, out of the pot and never out of another player's stake.
   ✅ A round that has opened keeps the beacon it was given, whatever the house does to the wait afterwards.
   ✅ The next round to open takes the new wait.
   🟡 The wait is sized against six weeks of measured Kadena blocks, where the average gap between blocks was 30 seconds and the longest was 136.
   🟡 If the chain stopped producing blocks for longer than the wait, one round would be exposed: the one open when it stopped, and only up to that round's own limit.
   ✅ The round's beacon is chosen at the moment the round opens, long before anyone can know what it says.
3. **The beacon is published, and the number falls out of it.**
   The beacon comes from a group of independent organisations that publish a new random value
   every 3 seconds, on their own network, with nothing to do with Kadena.
   ✅ Anyone at all settles the round by sending that beacon in, and a forged one is refused.
   ✅ A beacon never expires, so a round settles correctly however late it arrives.
4. **You collect, or you do not.**
   ✅ If you won, you claim. If you lost, you do nothing at all.
   ✅ Anyone can send that claim for you, and the money still goes to the account that placed the board.
   📋 The house's helper sends every winner's collection, so you need no KDA to be paid.
   📋 The helper runs on two machines, each with its own budget; if both stopped, a winner could still claim alone.
   🟡 Unclaimed winnings never expire, and nothing sweeps them to the house.

**Why not a Kadena block?** Because whoever produces a Kadena block sees what it would decide
before publishing it, and can throw it away and try again. A beacon produced somewhere else
cannot be thrown away by anyone here.

---

## What the house can and cannot do

🟡 The house sends no transaction inside a round and holds no secret of any kind.
✅ Nothing the house holds can reach a round that is already open.
✅ The house cannot change what a bet pays, or the wheel itself.

**Whose key it is.** The house key is Smart Pacts' own governance keyset: three hardware wallets,
of which **two must approve every single house action** — starting the contract, retuning the
table, taking the earnings out. There is no one-device path to any of them. Those same two
devices are the only ones who can put this contract on the chain at all, and the account the
earnings are paid into can be spent by nobody else either.

**What it can do, said plainly.**
🟡 The house can stop FUTURE rounds: by taking the spare capital out, by raising the minimum bet, or by lowering the share of the pot a round may risk.
✅ The share and the minimum stay the house's settings even after the contract is locked.
✅ The wait before the beacon stays the house's setting after the locking too, and its 60-second floor stays enforced.
✅ There is no ceiling on the minimum bet: the house chose control over a hard bound, so the table can be tuned for the whole life of the contract.
🟡 Every one of those acts is a public transaction on the chain that anyone can see.
✅ A raised minimum binds the next round and never the one already taking bets.

**Locking the contract.**
✅ Locking the contract changes one thing only: it can never be replaced again. Everything else keeps working exactly as it does now.
✅ A locked contract still takes bets, still settles, still pays winners and still refunds.
✅ The pot's capital is not stranded by locking the contract.
✅ Once it is locked, the route that lets the house key take the pot is refused by the contract's own governance, and the pot is untouched.

---

## If the beacon ever stops

✅ A stalled round refunds every stake and takes no fee at all.
✅ A refund opens only after 90 days in which nobody has shown the contract a beacon, and not a second earlier.
✅ A refund also needs evidence on the chain that beacons really stopped, so simply waiting out the clock buys a loser nothing.
✅ One cheap call, which anyone at all can send, shows the contract a beacon and resets that clock for every waiting round.
✅ That call settles nothing and moves no money.
✅ Once a later beacon is on the record, a round's refund is closed for good and the round must be settled instead.
That holds at the boundary too: a record exactly equal to the round's own beacon still closes it.

> 🔴 **The honest limits of that arrangement.**
>
> 🟡 If truly nobody acts for 90 days, a player who lost can take their stake back — and because a refund covers a whole round, a winner who never claimed would get their stake back instead of their winnings.
> 🟡 A round can stick for good if its own beacon becomes unreachable after the contract has already seen a later one; that round can be neither settled nor refunded, and its reserve stays locked.
> 📋 The whole of this rests on somebody making that cheap call inside the 90 days.
>
> **If you win, claim it.** You can always do that alone, from a value anybody can read.

## Who can call what

<!-- promise-gate:caller-legend -->
🟢 anyone · 🔵 the account whose money moves, with its signature · 🔴 the house's key
⚙️ normally reached only through another call of this contract; the house key can reach it
directly, and it then does exactly what that call would do
<!-- /promise-gate:caller-legend -->

### Playing

| | What it takes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 🔵 `bet` | Your account and your chips | Places one board. A board with no chips on it is refused. At most 24 chips go on one board. A chip of zero or less is refused. A bet the table does not offer is refused, never quietly ignored. |
| 🟢 `claim` | A round and the account that placed the board | Pays a winning board, or a refund from a stalled round. A board can only be claimed once. A board that did not win has nothing to claim. A round that has not settled yet cannot be claimed from. Nobody can claim a board they never placed. |

- A board below the table minimum is refused. The minimum is a house setting too, 0.01 KDA today, and it can never be set below 0.001 KDA — the floor is roughly twice what it costs the house to pay one winner.
- A board over the round's limit is refused.
- A contract-owned account cannot bet: it could never be paid back.
- A malformed account name cannot bet.

### Ending a round — open to everybody

| | What it takes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 🟢 `resolve` | A round and its beacon | Settles the round. Announces the winning number and the beacon it comes from. Pays the fee out of the pot in the same transaction. A round cannot be settled twice. A beacon for the wrong round does not verify. A re-encoded beacon cannot be used to pick a different number. |
| 🟢 `prove-liveness` | Any beacon | Shows the contract that beacons are still being published, and resets the refund clock for every waiting round. The record of beacons seen cannot be walked backwards. A forged beacon cannot raise it. Settling an older round does not move it backwards either. |
| 🟢 `void-round` | A stalled round | Opens the refund. Pays each player their whole stake back. A round that has settled can never then be refunded. Nothing stays locked once every round is settled. |

### The house's own calls

| | What it takes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 🔴 `initialize` | The account the earnings are paid to, and the pot's target size | Starts the contract, once and once only. The account must already exist, it cannot be the pot itself, and it cannot be a plain name a stranger could claim first. An account nobody could ever spend from is refused. |
| 🔴 `set-params` | The table limit, the minimum bet, the pot's target, the betting window and the wait before the beacon | Retunes the table for FUTURE rounds. Only the house key can retune the table or take money out. The betting window it sets can never be shorter than 30 seconds or longer than 1 hour. The share it sets can never be above the whole of the pot's spare capital. |
| 🔴 `withdraw-house` | An amount | Moves spare capital out of the pot to the account named at the start. |

### Putting capital in — open to everybody

| | What it takes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 🔵 `fund-house` | An account and an amount | Adds capital to the pot. 🟡 Anyone may strengthen the bank, and doing so grants no claim on it whatsoever. |

### Reading, which costs nothing and needs no key

| | What it takes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 🟢 `pot-status` | — | What the pot holds, what it has reserved, the fee right now, and the largest even-money board it would accept. The largest even-money board it advertises is one a bet actually takes. It is re-checked mid-round against the pot as it stands. Nothing is advertised when the only board that would fit is under the minimum. |
| 🟢 `get-round` | A round | Everything the round froze when it opened, and its result. |
| 🟢 `get-board` | A round and an account | That account's chips, its stake, and whether it has collected. |
| 🟢 `round-boards` | A round | Every board placed in that round, so whoever is paying the winners can find them. It reads and nothing else: it moves no money and writes nothing down. |
| 🟢 `get-params` | — | The table's current settings and the highest beacon the contract has seen. |
| 🟢 `house-account` | — | The pot's account name. Anyone can work it out, and nobody can take that name under their own key. |
| 🟢 `pot-guard` | — | The lock the pot's account is built from. Anyone can work the same value out from a transaction alone, so having it hands over nothing. |

### Inside the contract

| | What it takes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| ⚙️ `open-round` | — | Opens the next round on the terms the game row holds; nothing can be passed in. |

### Plumbing — the contract's building blocks

Everything on a public blockchain is public, so these can all be *called* by anyone — but they
exist for the contract's own use. Each one answers a question, works something out without
writing it down, or refuses a bad input. **None of them can move money or write a record.** They
are listed so this page accounts for every function in the contract, with nothing invisible.

| | What it is for |
|---|---|
| `winning-bets` · `payout-mult` | The rules of European roulette, written out: which bets win on each number, and what each one pays. A single number pays 35 to 1; red, black, odd, even, high and low pay 1 to 1. |
| `board-payout` · `own-vector` · `prep` | What a board is owed on a given number, and what it would be owed on each of the 37 pockets in turn. |
| `validate-entries` | Checks every chip on a board and adds up the stake. |
| `fee-rate` | The fee the pot is charging right now, from how full the pot is. |
| `vmax` | The largest number in a list — how the worst pocket is found. |
| `curr-time` | The chain's own clock. It is the previous block's time. |
| `rkey` · `bkey` | How the contract builds its record keys — rounds · boards. |

## What is not built, or not true today

- ⛔ **A locked contract.**

---

## True of the whole thing

1. ✅ **The wheel depends on one other contract, the beacon verifier, pinned to its exact code**:
   against any other code, this contract refuses to load at all.
   ✅ That verifier can never be replaced, so the dependency cannot change underneath a locked wheel.
   🟡 It holds no money, keeps no records and has no key of its own.
2. The wheel is the official European wheel: 37 pockets, one green, eighteen red and eighteen black.
   The table offers 158 distinct bets, every one of them an official European bet. None of them is missing.
   Every bet pays the official multiple for the numbers it covers.
   Zero is in no red, black, odd, even, high, low, dozen or column bet.
   The table the contract settles from agrees with the rules on all 158 bets across all 37 numbers.
3. The table's chain is **chain 2**: the chain where the earnings account already holds its
   balance, and where Smart Pacts' other live contract already runs.
   📋 **The contract runs on a chain that carried none of its records when it started.**
   📋 **The account the earnings are paid to exists and is spendable** — the contract refused to
   start until it could be paid, but it cannot tell whose an account is.
4. Gas is small: even a full board of chips costs far less than one block allows.
   A claim fits inside the gas ceiling a sponsor would set for it.
   A bet is never sponsored — a player funds their own stake, always.
5. The books balance after every kind of settlement, checked independently of the contract's own
   bookkeeping.
6. The house's upgrade authority, `GOVERNANCE`, backs nothing else at all, which is
   why locking the contract changes only whether it can be replaced. Its day-to-day authority,
   `ADMIN`, is a separate permission and keeps working afterwards.
